Theme

Nature & food

flash noun and verb

of light

also flashing, a flash of light, glitter, gleam, sparkle

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.71 (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 2.1.19: armōrum (Lewis & Short)

fulgor, fulgōris m.

noun, third declension

a flash, gleam, glitter

(in this sense mostly poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short))

First a flash of lightning (Lucr., Verg.; in prose fulgur, see lightning); then any flash or gleam, of arms, of a lamp, of the sun.

Other words

  • micō, micāre, micuī — flash, glitter, twinkle; quiver

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 6.12.9: gladiī (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 3.439 (Lewis & Short)

    Of anything that moves quickly to and fro: a beating pulse, a darting tongue, flashing swords, twinkling stars (Lewis & Short).

  • coruscō, coruscāre — flash, quiver; brandish

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 8.661; 12.431 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica: Verg., Ov.)

    Poetic: to shake or brandish (spears), and of flames and lightning, to flash.

Examples

  • cujus fulgōre collūcēre atque illūstrārī Jovis templum oportēbat

    whose flashing light was to make Jupiter’s temple shine and blaze (of a jewelled candelabrum)Cic. Verr. 2.4.71 (Lewis & Short)

  • Vidēsne lūmen illud procul micāns?

    Can you see that light flashing in the distance?composed

See also lightning, bright, torch.

SourcesLewis & Short: fulgor · Lewis & Short: mico · Lewis & Short: corusco
